questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state.

questions.stem: High glucose draws water into the blood and lowers the measured sodium. Corrected sodium = measured sodium + 1.6 x ((glucose - 100) / 100). What is the client's corrected sodium? Record your answer as a whole number.

rationale.correct: 150 + 1.6 x ((980 - 100) / 100) = 150 + 1.6 x 8.8 = 150 + 14.1 = 164 mEq/L. The client's true free water deficit is larger than the measured sodium suggests.

content.template: The client's most urgent problem is {{b1}}. The main danger of correcting it too fast is {{b2}}.

options.text: severe dehydration with hyperosmolality
ketoacidosis
hyperkalemia

cerebral edema from a rapid fall in osmolality
hypertension

perOption.b1:a: HHS causes fluid losses of around 9 L in adults.
perOption.b1:d: The drowsiness fits hyperosmolality; no focal signs are described.
perOption.b2:a: Brain cells adapt to high osmolality; a fast fall pulls water into them.
perOption.b2:c: Not the danger of correcting too fast.

questions.stem: For each part of the plan, indicate whether it is indicated or contraindicated.

rows.text: 0.9% sodium chloride 1 L in the first hour

Add dextrose to the IV fluid when glucose reaches about 300 mg/dL

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The anion gap is {{b1}}. The near-normal glucose is explained by {{b2}}, and the trigger was {{b3}}.

rationale.correct: A high-gap ketoacidosis with near-normal glucose after surgery and fasting is SGLT2 inhibitor-associated euglycemic DKA.

perOption.b2:a: SGLT2 inhibitors lower glucose while ketones build up.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
